subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class one-line localhost plus Telegram owner bootstrap surface, and should it live in non-interactive onboarding, a dedicated bootstrap command, or plugin-owned setup hooks?
rationale: The request crosses install/service lifecycle, dashboard auth, channel credentials, and Telegram owner authorization, so the public API and trust boundary need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Design first-class bootstrap
options.body: Define a supported setup surface that preserves numeric allowlist/owner trust semantics and then implement it across onboarding, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to Telegram owner setup
options.body: Keep this umbrella as context while narrower Telegram owner/allowlist issues carry the first implementation step.

options.title: Defer wrapper surface
options.body: Leave setup terminal-first for now and document the secure manual composition instead of adding a convenience wrapper.

recommendation.title: Design first-class bootstrap
recommendation.body: Define a supported setup surface that preserves numeric allowlist/owner trust semantics and then implement it across onboarding, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current code-history signal across onboarding, Telegram setup, and setup-wizard product boundaries.
